title: Cohomological smoothness of smooth morphisms
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
for every smooth separated morphism $f:X\to Y$ of relative dimension
$d$ put

$$
\omega_f\;=\;Rf^!\Lambda_Y.
$$

Then:

1. *Tensor formula.* For every $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ the
canonical map
$$
Lf^*K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}\omega_f\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf^!K
$$
is an isomorphism.
1. *Invertibility.* $\omega_f$ is invertible.
1. *Base change.* The formation of $\omega_f$ and of the
canonical map is compatible with arbitrary base change: for a
Cartesian square with $f'$ the base change of $f$,
$$
Lu^*\omega_f\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\omega_{f'},
$$
and the two canonical maps correspond under $Lu^*$; this holds for
*arbitrary* $v$ by [lem-pur-smb-extraordinary].
1. *Composition.* The tensor formula is compatible with
composition of smooth morphisms, through the composition isomorphism
for $R^!$ of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image].

(*Orientation-free form*: none of the four statements identifies
$\omega_f$ with a twist and a shift; that identification,
$\omega_f\cong\Lambda(d)[2d]$, is the content of
[thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object] proved below from the diagonal
argument.)

proof.text: The finite coefficient setting supplies HasInvertibleExponent on X. Use the existing ordinary-etale smooth duality theorem: the dualizing object is a shifted locally constant rank-one sheaf and every canonical tensor map is invertible. Its proof follows the affine-space model and etale descent, so no orientation is chosen.

source.place: Both paragraphs; canonical etale comparison-coordinate proof

proof.text: Take a tensor inverse of the etale dualizing object. Exact monoidal site comparison, with the unit comparison of lem-pur-shifted-line-site-inverse, carries both evaluations to inverse evaluations for the compared dualizing object. A tensor-invertible object is dualizable. Since X is noetherian, the existing constructibleFiniteTor_of_isDualizable theorem puts the compared inverse in Dctf. This proves the required invertibility clause. The tensor clause is the image of the already invertible etale tensor map.

source.place: Both paragraphs; canonical etale comparison-coordinate proof

proof.text: For an arbitrary Cartesian square use ordinary-etale smooth exceptional base change and specialize its invertibility to the unit-normalized dualizing map. For the tensor equation, projection/exchange compatibility gives the mate identity for the two-variable adjoint tensor map. Specializing its first variable to the unit and using naturality and the left-unitor identity gives the displayed dualizing tensor equation. Apply comparison pullback to this equality. The private helper is the arbitrary-square form of the calculation in prop-asd-smooth-base-change.

source.place: Both paragraphs; canonical etale comparison-coordinate proof

proof.text: For composition retain exactly the defined compactification tower and its three common-refinement comparisons. Projection maps are invariant under the comparisons. The explicit compactification-tower projection theorem therefore proves ProjectionCompCompatible for smoothCompactSupportCompIso. Taking the unique right-adjoint comparison gives the composition identity for the two-variable exceptional tensor maps. This calculation is the split statement lem-v8-smooth-tensor-composition-equation, whose own proof uses lem-amb-compactification-projection-composition and lem-route-projection-map-associativity.

source.place: Both paragraphs; canonical etale comparison-coordinate proof

proof.text: Specialize the composition identity at the coefficient unit. Naturality of the adjoint comparison cancels its inverse in the defined dualizing comparison q. Associativity of the projection tensor map and the left-unitor identity then identify the result with the reassociated tensor of the two dualizing tensor maps. These are private formal calculations, retaining every comparison arrow in the original statement. The smooth tensor theorem makes q invertible; applying exact comparison gives the required pro-etale equation.

proof.text:
Work for a finite coefficient ring. The earlier orientation-free
theorem [thm-asd-smooth-tensor] proves the canonical tensor
formula on the ordinary etale site and shows that
$\omega_f[-2d]$ is a locally constant free rank-one sheaf.
In particular it is tensor-invertible, and tensoring it with the
pullback of a bounded constructible finite-Tor complex stays in that
category. The actual-adjoint comparison
[thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] and
[thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] transport the tensor map and
its isomorphy to the finite etale-origin objects used here.
Because the map is obtained by transposing the projection formula
and counit on both sites, the transported map is the canonical
$\theta_{f,K}$ in [def-pur-co-smoothness].

For the third condition of that definition,
[lem-pur-smb-extraordinary] proves arbitrary base change of the
actual right adjoint, and [prop-asd-smooth-base-change] also
proves its compatibility with the tensor transformation before
transport. Thus these are all three conditions of cohomological
smoothness. For composition, [lem-pur-co-smooth-composition]
identifies $\omega_{gf}$ with
$\omega_f\otimes^LLf^*\omega_g$. The two tensor transformations
agree: transposing them gives the projection formula followed by
the same two counits, composed in their adjunction order. This
proves the fourth assertion without using an orientation of $f$.
